meta.title: TheyDo case study: 8.6% more productive | Innerleaps
meta.description: Would mental training feel like a sign of weakness? TheyDo's CEO feared so. Then 39 people signed up voluntarily, and productivity rose 8.6%.

hero.title: 8.6% <0>more productive</0> and 7 in 10 feel <0>less stress</0>
hero.subtitle: TheyDo works fully remote, with lots of freedom. That leaves little visibility into how the team works. 39 colleagues took part and trained their attention for six weeks.
hero.quote: You're enabling people to get more out of their workday without working more hours.
hero.photoAlt: Jochem van der Veer, CEO of TheyDo, during the interview

stats.label: for the trainers, 8.1 for the programme

items.label: Company
items.value: TheyDo, journey management software for large enterprises

items.label: Participants
items.value: 39 employees, about 40% of the company, signed up voluntarily

items.label: Programme
items.value: Six weeks of Innerleaps brain training, online, March to April 2026

items.label: Measured
items.value: Before the training and four weeks after it, plus an evaluation at the end of the training

context.title: What was going on at <0>TheyDo</0>?
context.quote: We're a remote organisation with employees in 26 countries. We're seeing them on screen time, but outside of it, we don't know.

doubts.title: What were your <0>doubts</0> before you started?
doubts.quote: It could be seen as a sign of weakness. I wasn't sure how our employees would respond. It could be backfiring. But in the end, it didn't.
doubts.fact: 39 people signed up voluntarily. About 40% of the company.
doubts.bridge: Why did it work? Jochem presented it as maintenance, not repair.

colleagues.title: What did you notice in your <0>colleagues</0>?
colleagues.quote: A coworker just blurted out: it's so great, I'm actually sleeping again. That's not something you talk about at work.
colleagues.intro: 22 of the 39 participants filled in an evaluation at the end. These came up most:

investment.title: Was it worth the <0>investment</0>?
investment.quote: It's a hell yes. In our sales team, 8.6% literally turns into more meetings, more qualified prospects and ultimately more revenue.
investment.fact: At TheyDo, the programme paid for itself from a productivity gain of 0.36%. The measured gain was 8.6%. Where your break-even sits depends on your salaries. <0>Calculate it for your team</0>.

hr.title: How much <0>work</0> was it for HR?
hr.quote: It was a [fair] amount of work, but that's because we cared. You guys were super organised. You told me exactly what to do and when to do it.
hr.fact: A bonus for a remote team: colleagues got to know each other properly.

better.title: What could have been <0>better</0>?
better.quote: It wasn't about scepticism. I think it was about framing.
items: We now say upfront that you'll need a quiet spot
The workbook arrives week by week, not in one go
English audio re-recorded by a native speaker
A daily nudge in your own chat app

again.title: Would you do it <0>again</0>?
again.quote: I would definitely do this again. Not only because of the data, but because my employees said: this was a great programme, it helped me.
again.fact: As far as research has looked, yes. Studies up to a year after the training still found measurably less stress. Longer than that has hardly been studied.

know.title: How do we <0>know</0> this?
items: We measured productivity with the World Health Organization's Health and Work Performance Questionnaire (HPQ). 20 participants rated their own work performance over the past four weeks: once before the training, and again four weeks after it ended.
At the end, 22 of the 39 participants filled in an evaluation.
People who practised more than once a week did even better: their productivity rose by 11.1%.
Every participant got their own impact report. Individual answers never go to the employer.
know.sources: Sources: Kessler et al. (2003, 2004) for the HPQ. Michaelsen et al. (2023) for how long the effect lasts.
